steps.name: Restless Soldier
steps.text: (Yawns)

steps.name: Cautious Soldier
steps.text: Look sharp. We're on shift for another two hours.

steps.name: Restless Soldier
steps.text: Blyat... not a damn mangler in this ice and snow.

spans.text: ... not a damn mangler in this ice and snow.

steps.name: Cautious Soldier
steps.text: Hey... did you hear something?

steps.name: Restless Soldier
steps.text: What—
The soldier turns around, only to see a crossbow bolt punching through his friend's skull.

steps.name: Restless Soldier
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Restless Soldier
steps.text: Ah! Ahhhh—!

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Rankin! We got the ones below! Let's go up!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Wait! Don't be rash! Come back!
The miners are gathered under the outpost, gazing at the flashing warning light above their heads.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Watch your heads!

steps.name: Miner A & Miner B
steps.text: Mmph! Ugh!

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: They saw us! They're pulling the ladder!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We'll have to do this the hard way.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Take all the explosives and come with me, Team 3. We're blowing the outpost door, whatever it takes.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Don't stop if I fall. Take my place.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Team 4, Team 5, keep shooting and cover us!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: The rest of you, don't let a single soldier get away.

steps.name: Miner C & Miner D
steps.text: You got it!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: On my mark—
The searchlight catches them, and it is immediately followed by a hail of projectiles.
Rankin continues to push forward towards the outpost, raising his crossbow and taking aim at the vexing searchlight above their heads.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Argh—!
Suddenly, Rankin feels a sharp pain on his forehead, and the left side of his field of vision is covered in red.
Blood streams down. He hears a ringing in his head.

steps.name: Worried Miner
steps.text: Rankin? Rankin!

steps.name: Staunch Miner
steps.text: Not a step back! With me! Push forward!

steps.name: Angry Miner
steps.text: Damn it. We're dead anyway if we go back! Might as well take a few of them down with us!
The cries around him seem so distant. He can hear the sound of crossbow bolts finding flesh. He can hear the sound of bodies hitting the floor.
He must not fall. Not when victory is so close.
He wills his limbs to move with the last bit of strength he has left, once again raising his crossbow, aiming at that loathsome light above. He pulls the trigger.

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: They're weakening! Keep up!

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: Now, ready—

steps.name: Staunch Miner
steps.text: The door's blown! Charge!
The miners' voices feel more and more distant. It is all Rankin can do to keep up.
No one notices him in this battle of life and death.
He leans against the rubble and heads upwards, one small step at a time.
His senses are returning, and his body is getting used to the pain.
He walks over bodies that were alive just a moment ago. The spiral staircase leads to an aperture at the top, where the most beautiful aurora of the Ursine night shines through.
He remembers sitting in the mine elevators, gazing up at the only light above.
Finally, the last step. He finds himself standing amidst the aurora, beneath the stars, with friends.

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: Rankin?! Are you alright??

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: ...I'm fine.
Rankin wipes away the blood on his forehead and takes a look at his brothers and sisters around him.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Half of us didn't make it...

steps.name: Staunch Miner
steps.text: ...But we did it.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We did it...
In the distance, Deity Grypherburg remains hidden behind the thick taiga. The vast, frozen icy lake seems to taunt them for their foolish challenge.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We climbed from the dark mines to the surface, and now we stand atop the Army's outpost.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We will cross the frozen lake and forest, and plant our flags in even more places.
Rankin's eyes burn bright as he tries to communicate his vision to the others.
Their faces are bright with the joy of victory too. They have waited for this day for far too long.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Nikto, we finally—
Rankin turns around, but does not see the familiar figure.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: ...Nikto?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...
I ran away when the first bolt left the crossbow.
It's no shame to be afraid. It is only the most foolish of fools who do not know fear.
Rankin is mad. Everyone who follows him is mad.
I wanted to pull them back. But if they want to die, let them.
I can't die yet.
From cobbler to tutor, to being adopted by a count. I didn't do all that just so that I could die in a place like that.
Die, and it's all over.
I must survive.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Volgrad is just ahead...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: ...Start over, Nikto.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Blyat...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: What the bloody hell is that...?

steps.name: Staunch Miner
steps.text: A torch!

steps.name: Staunch Miner
steps.text: We should light a torch, so that the others will know we've succeeded and come to meet up with us!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Yes... you're right.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Light the fire.
A dull thud coming from the distance shakes the icefields, and makes their eardrums and hearts tremble.

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: What's that?!

steps.name: Staunch Miner
steps.text: O-Over there!
They look in the direction that he is pointing, and see a massive battleship rising on the horizon, so massive it is hard to tell whether it is a ship or a nomadic city.
The taiga is leveled in an instant, and the stars are veiled by red light.
Snow and tree trunks are torn to pieces and sucked into the sky.
Only now...
Only now do they understand what they are dealing with.
Ursus.
They are dealing with Ursus.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: So this is what it is...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Raidian?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I just got a message on a public channel.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: It says that the Ursine ore veins are near exhausted...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: The Armies are trying to cover it up. At least one army is already here in the Far North...!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Did the Doctor's team send the message?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Uncertain, but likely. This is a warning from the Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The mines becoming exhausted... could it be...?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But I don't understand. Ursus wants to cover it up? Do they plan on killing everyone in the Far North who knows about it?!

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...I knew it.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The rumors of the ore veins running dry were true... That's the source of all the unusual events. That's what they're trying to hide!

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: You don't look surprised.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It was the worst-case scenario that I projected, until now.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: But now, there is reason to believe it's true. And I have no doubt some of the Army brass are capable of doing such things...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The Far North is the most dangerous place on Terra right now. We must leave, immediately.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We haven't made contact with the Doctor yet—

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: They sent us a warning. They're in a better position to be informed than we are.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: There's no guarantee that we would find them if we went back now. We would only be wasting our time.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Mon3tr can protect the Doctor. They're less likely to be targeted than a large group.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: But if the Armies have come to cover this up on the government's behalf, how can we be sure that Grypherburg is a safe place to go?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You still don't trust me.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...We do need to make sure that...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: 'Kal'tsit.'

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The name once again came to the government's attention not long ago. This mysterious figure has left too many unusual traces on Ursus, and across all of Terra.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Information about her is considered top-secret in Ursus. For this reason, some of us harbor hope that she can answer certain questions that Ursus is facing right now.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...Who are you, really?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Perhaps a re-introduction is in order...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Eloysius Vasilyevna Gorchekova, Lieutenant of the Tsar's Battalion, Ursine Imperial Guard. I answer to... Chairman Islam Witte of the State Council.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: My orders are to investigate reports of mutated Infected and associated incidents in the Central Mining District of the Far North, and...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...To make contact with Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I know it's a little late to claim sincerity, and it's true that I had intended to keep this a secret.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Whether you believe it or not, however, I can tell you that I could have dealt with you in Bresk, if I had any ill intent.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: This is not the sort of cooperation that Rhodes Island seeks, but I can understand your position.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Let's set the argument aside for now... what's your plan, Eloysius?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I have vehicles on the southwest shore of Lake Neva, about ten kilometers from here.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It's not much, but it should be enough to take everyone away from here.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I can hide them in a village outside Grypherburg, then find a way to get you inside the city under the government's protection.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Mantra said that the people here are still under the influence of the Yurodstvo. We need to free them from its control first.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: She can find the Yurodstvo, but not a way to deal with it?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I have no desire to witness a tragedy, but my duty comes first. I must ensure that someone is alive to bring word back to Grypherburg.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: If you insist on getting everyone out of here safely...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I can give you one hour, no more.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Understood. I will make it quick.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: I think I've made a breakthrough.
Mantra carefully projects her perception into every corner.
She identifies one little fluctuation amidst all the numb, unmoving thoughts.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...Babushka...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Let's go... let's leave here... alright?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: If you stand up, everyone will... follow.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: We'll go south, to Deity Grypherburg, or... anywhere, just not...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Just not here.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...Okay?
Vetochki takes a knee before the illusion that she believes to be her grandmother. She takes the hands that do not exist to Mantra's eyes, and rubs her cheeks against them.
It is only when she sees the tears on the girl's face that Mantra realizes how frightening this trust is. The girl continues to do so, even without getting any response.
Mantra remembers Raidian's words.
'Vetochki's parents were executed for organizing a strike. Her grandmother is her only family now.'
'It seems as though everyone in the mining district knew Nadia, including the guards.'
'They sought her assistance more than they sought the medical team's. They sought comfort when they were in pain, insight when they were lost, and found a strange peace in her words.'
'...I should have noticed that something wasn't right. I thought she was just a respected old woman.'

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Please, babushka...
Mantra watches the girl before her, and gently makes her own voice appear in the girl's mind.
She believes you will find peace here.
Once all hope is gone.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Who—
Vetochki.
Vetochki turns around to see the Phidia standing behind her.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Y-You know, my name? But I never, told you...

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: In this place, at least, you should be able to express yourself clearly.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: But you're talking in the same way that you usually do, which means that you've not been seriously affected...

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Perhaps there's still a way for you to wake up.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Is Nadia your family?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Yes, she's... she's my babushka.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: And my only, family.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Are you sure?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Of course I am. She's my, babushka.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Your babushka wants everyone to endure their pain.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: So that they have no desire to live, nor choose to end their own pain and die.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: No, no—babushka wouldn't!

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: She's just tired, like everyone... Everyone's just, tired.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: We want to live. Of course we do! But there's always people, who don't want us to...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Always someone...

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Who?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Th-The Patrol Units.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: You defeated the Patrol Units.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Th-The guards, and, the people, in the lab.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: They're not here.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I, I—

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Who else doesn't want you to live?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: The black... monster...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: And... and...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Why? I... I can't remember...

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Let me ask again.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Are you holding the hands of your family?

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Turn around, Vetochki.
Vetochki does not want to turn around. As long as she does not do so, those cold and withered hands will forever remain the way they are.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Tell me. What do you see?
Don't turn around. Don't turn around. Don't turn around.
She keeps telling herself.
But she turned around.
Babushka is in front of her. Babushka is singing a lullaby.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I... I see Babushka Nadia.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: No. Look more closely.
Babushka is in front of her. Her hands are cold.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: What do you see?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I see... circle. I see—

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Red.
Vetochki frantically shakes her head.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Why...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Why is it always red?
Babushka sitting, babushka standing, babushka, colors ever-changing.
Babushka lying in a pool of blood, deciding that Vetochki may die.

steps.name: Picky Woman
steps.text: Brrr. Is this what autumn is like in Ursus? I would hate to see what they call winter.

steps.name: Picky Woman
steps.text: An open-air party, with no lawn or picnic table? What are you inviting us here to see?

steps.name: Eager Man
steps.text: Entertainment you don't get in Kazimierz, no matter how rich you are.

steps.name: Picky Woman
steps.text: A few lives and deaths, big deal. I doubt those miners we saw on the way could give us a show that measures up to knightsports.

steps.name: Eager Man
steps.text: The knights fight every year, but Breskenoy hasn't seen a single death sentence in a decade under the rule of the current Grand Duchess! This is a truly rare event.

steps.name: Picky Woman
steps.text: Death sentence? Who's the criminal?

steps.name: Eager Man
steps.text: A miner couple caught in the act, plotting to organize an Infected strike.

steps.name: Picky Woman
steps.text: My, my, how awful...

steps.name: Eager Man
steps.text: Yes. It was such a horrendous crime that the Grand Duchess apparently wept when she signed the death warrant.

steps.name: Eager Man
steps.text: But there is no precedence for humane death sentences in these parts. It's easy to bury them in the nearby swamps, but it would be such a waste of a rare death sentence, wouldn't it?

steps.name: Eager Man
steps.text: Which is why we're here.

steps.name: Eager Man
steps.text: The procedures start with whipping. I heard paying guests like us even get to pick the whip, add blades to it, soak it in brine...

steps.name: Picky Woman
steps.text: What if they died sooner than planned and their rocks exploded in front of us? I had this dress made just for this trip, you know.

steps.name: Eager Man
steps.text: That won't be a problem! Their infection isn't that bad. It would have taken them years to die if they didn't commit their crime.

steps.name: Eager Man
steps.text: As for the party and picnic that you asked about, you'll see it soon enough.

steps.name: Eager Man
steps.text: Now, let's get ourselves warm by the fire.

steps.name: Impatient Guard
steps.text: Are they still breathing?

steps.name: Soldier On Duty
steps.text: Th-The woman's still babbling treason...

steps.name: Impatient Guard
steps.text: Is the man dead?

steps.name: Soldier On Duty
steps.text: Cut his tongue out yesterday.

steps.name: Impatient Guard
steps.text: Why not cut the woman's too?

steps.name: Soldier On Duty
steps.text: Th-The guests yesterday said no.

steps.name: Soldier On Duty
steps.text: They wanted to hear her scream—

steps.name: Impatient Guard
steps.text: Did she?

steps.name: Soldier On Duty
steps.text: No! Not even once. She keep repeating her 'petitions', saying things like 'for the other children who died in the mines'...

steps.name: Soldier On Duty
steps.text: Couldn't understand a word of it! She must be mad.

steps.name: Impatient Guard
steps.text: Wouldn't have tried to start a strike if she wasn't.

steps.name: Impatient Guard
steps.text: *sigh* Cut the woman's tongue too.

steps.name: Soldier On Duty
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Impatient Guard
steps.text: And that kid. She was standing there yesterday too, wasn't she?

steps.name: Soldier On Duty
steps.text: Yes. The constable wanted her to stand there and watch, until her parents breathe their last.

steps.name: Impatient Guard
steps.text: Then send her back to the quarters once they're dead.

steps.name: Soldier On Duty
steps.text: I'm afraid she has to go down to the mines with her mom's lamp and ID. She was born in a mine, you know, which makes her a miner too.

steps.name: Impatient Guard
steps.text: ...Does she have a lamp? Do you see a lamp in her hands?

steps.name: Soldier On Duty
steps.text: N-No, sir!

steps.name: Impatient Guard
steps.text: Then send her back to the quarters once it's done, mudak!

spans.text: Then send her back to the quarters once it's done,

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: Vetochki... here, take these. Butter, minced meat, chocolate... Good girl.

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: D-Don't get any wrong ideas! It wasn't my husband who sold your parents out! I earned these myself, pushing the carts in the mines!

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: There's only you and your babushka now. Take care of her, alright?

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: Tell her she doesn't need to return the scissors she borrowed. Come find me if you ever need anything...

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: I'll do what I can to help.

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: *sigh* My kid would be around your age, if she had lived.
She said some other things, but I never answered.
Was it because I couldn't talk, or because I had already walked away and went home?
All I know is that I saw red—
Red dripping on greyish-white plastic.
I thought I was back outside at that place again... but no.
It was babushka.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Argh—ahhhh!

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Ugh...
Yesterday, and today. I learned that the red inside a human body isn't endless. It will dry up. It makes people hurt. It brings death.
So I tried to stop the red that was flowing out, with my hands, like the game that I played with my friends when I was little.
'Whoever picks up the most water has the most happiness.'
'Whoever bags the most winds has the most freedom.'

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: *Sob* *sob*—

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: No—no, no!
I can't keep it.
I must keep it.
I can't—

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Babushka...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Babushka.
The cold body sinks into the plastic, into the mud, before my eyes. I look up and see 'it'.
A pale, standing shadow.
I cried—

steps.name: Nadia?
steps.text: I'm here.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...You told me to, endure, and forgive.

steps.name: Nadia?
steps.text: To survive, yes.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Must we still, endure?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Endure, and share, other pain, only leads to death now.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Do we endure... for nothing?

steps.name: Nadia?
steps.text: Desire anything, and you will only sin. Your suffering soul needs eternal peace.

steps.name: Nadia?
steps.text: Come, child. Come into my embrace.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...Did you forgive too?

steps.name: Nadia?
steps.text: I forgave.

steps.name: Nadia?
steps.text: We must accept the life that Ursus has granted, as we accept the death that Ursus has granted. We must not choose. We must not struggle.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Did you forgive? For killing mom, and dad... your own, child.

steps.name: Nadia?
steps.text: Yes, I forgive.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: 'I forgive'?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Then... no.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You're not Babushka Nadia.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Babushka wouldn't, forgive like this. Not forgive for peace.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: She won't forgive. She won't endure. She's dead... buried.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You're not her.

steps.name: Nadia?
steps.text: I am.
I am—
I am?
■■, submit to ■■...
Or... ■■ destruction.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Step back, Vetochki!

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Sh-She's not! She's not, Babushka Nadia.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: No, she's not.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: But if, she's not, babushka...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Who is she?
The light of Arts floats around Mantra. She has made the foe reveal its true colors.
But it is not yet over. She must continue to build a barrier in the cognitive space, to isolate herself and the entity before her from other people.
In the meantime, she continues to communicate the truth.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: 'Yurodstvo.'

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: This is the Yurodstvo that you asked about. It is a demonic creation that has been given this name.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Perhaps it was once human. Now, it is a far cry from the concept of human.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I don't understand...

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: You don't have to.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: I never understood its true nature, even though there was a chance, however minute, that I might have become it.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: You saw it at the wrong time and called to it. That's all.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: The wrong time?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: So... it was wrong, from the beginning?

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: It's not your fault, Vetochki.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: I'll take over from here.
